job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let's clear up some common confusion about heat. Rohan, if you touch a metal spoon and a wooden spoon in this room, why does the metal one feel colder? Rohan: I think metal is naturally colder than wood. Teacher: Actually, they are at the same room temperature. Metal just conducts heat away from your hand faster than wood. Priya, what happens when we use a laboratory thermometer? Priya: We should take it out of the liquid quickly to read the temperature before it changes. Teacher: That is a common mistake. You must keep the bulb inside the liquid while reading, or the temperature will drop immediately. Also, remember that heat is energy in transit, not a substance like 'cold' that flows into objects. When you hold a hot cup, heat moves from the cup to your hand. Finally, consider convection in air. Heat does not just travel upwards; it moves in currents wherever fluid can circulate. If you feel warmth near a heater, it is because air molecules are transferring energy through these currents, not because heat has a specific direction it must follow. Understanding these principles helps us see how energy truly behaves in our daily lives.

items.evidence: Metal just conducts heat away from your hand faster than wood.
items.q: A metal spoon and a wooden spoon sit in one room. Why does the metal one feel colder?
options: It pulls warmth from your hand more quickly
It is naturally at a lower temperature than wood
It sends cold flowing into your hand
It sends its heat upward, away from you
items.explain: Both spoons are at room temperature; metal just carries heat away from your hand faster.

wrong.why: thinks metal is naturally colder than wood
thinks cold is a substance that flows into objects

items.evidence: You must keep the bulb inside the liquid while reading, or the temperature will drop immediately.
items.q: Priya lifts a thermometer out of hot water to read it. What goes wrong?
options: The reading drops as the bulb leaves the liquid
The reading becomes more accurate in open air
The reading rises because the air is warmer
The reading stays the same after it leaves
items.explain: The temperature drops immediately once the bulb is out, so the bulb must stay in the liquid.

wrong.why: thinks the thermometer must be taken out to read it
thinks leaving the liquid changes nothing

items.evidence: Also, remember that heat is energy in transit, not a substance like 'cold' that flows into objects.
items.q: A drink becomes cooler when ice is added. Which explains this?
options: Heat energy moves from the drink to the ice
Cold flows from the ice into the drink
Temperature moves from the drink into the ice
Heat only moves upward, out of the drink
items.explain: Heat is energy in transit that leaves the drink; no substance called cold flows into it.

wrong.why: thinks cold is a substance that flows in
treats heat and temperature as the same thing

items.evidence: If you feel warmth near a heater, it is because air molecules are transferring energy through these currents, not because heat has a specific direction it must follow.
items.q: You feel warmth beside a heater, not only above it. How is this possible?
options: Air currents carry energy in every direction
Heat can only travel upward from a heater
Cold air flows away, leaving warmth behind
Hot particles travel along the floor to you
items.explain: Air molecules transfer energy through currents, and heat has no single direction it must follow.

wrong.why: treats cold as something that moves away
thinks particles travel from the hot end to the cold end

items.evidence: When you hold a hot cup, heat moves from the cup to your hand.
items.q: Why do your fingers feel warm when you hold a hot cup?
options: Heat moves from the cup to your fingers
Heat moves from your fingers to the cup
The cup's temperature is poured into your fingers
The cup is naturally warmer than other objects
items.explain: Heat moves from the hot cup into your hand, which makes your fingers feel warm.

wrong.why: reverses the direction of heat flow
thinks heat and temperature are the same thing
blames the cup's material, not heat movement
